newsitem.title: UK: LME ends mixed, clouds gather over sentiment.
newsitem.headline: LME ends mixed, clouds gather over sentiment.

text.p: Base metal prices ended an uncertain Tuesday LME session mixed, although market-leaders copper and aluminium were softer with sentiment turning negative, traders said.
Elsewhere, the volatile nickel market was firmer, tin continued its correction, but lead and zinc were unimpressive as summer slowdown factors held sway.
"The mood and the good sentiment has disappeared from the metals," one said.
Nickel was the major mover today, and trading remained volatile during the afternoon. Prices continued to whip around, albeit above support levels to finally end at $7,180, up $155.
Traders said the wide price moves were due to opposite fundamental developments, with overnight news of the strike at Inco's Sudbury facilities driving the market higher.

Subsequent news that Russia's Norilsk was looking at a 20 percent increase in production this year took the heat out of the rally. But in the short-term, caution over the Inco strike is likely to restrict the downside, they said.
Copper also fluctuated throughout the session, but in a tighter range and mostly towards the lower end of the band.
There was reasonable support around $2,470/75 again, but a covering rally in mid-afternoon was soundly rebuffed around $2,500.
"These bounces are getting smaller and not too convincing," the trader said.
Talk that China may be a seller of copper, rather than a hoped-for buyer, was an unnerving factor, with some saying stocks may rise in the Far East soon.
Last three months trade was at $2,479, down $6 from the previous kerb. Cash/threes was marginally softer at $56/60 backwardation.

Aluminium was pummelled by fund liquidation and spread lending operations, against a background of increased availability in Europe. Again, the market was unwilling to hold a key upside level at $1,600, and by the close prices were back at $1,578, an $18 loss.
In lead, there was little significant action, with price movements dictated by the overall trend. Last business was at an unchanged $626.

Zinc met good buying ahead of a test of anticipated support around $1,310/15, although there continues to be concern over Chinese deliveries in Singapore. Nevertheless, last trade was at $1,334, up $4 from Monday.
Tin continued to build on Monday's corrective rally from 14-1/2 month lows, helped by the upturn in consumer business those levels fostered.
However, the market is wary of talk of Russian stockpile metal being shipped to the West. Last trade was at $5,680, up $40.
The alloy market was stable, and closed at $1,475/80 a tonne.
